questions.title: What are Edm.Boolean, Edm.Decimal and Edm.DateTime, and how are their values written in a request URI?
questions.description: Edm.Boolean represents binary-valued logic; its literal form is true or false. Edm.Decimal represents numeric values with fixed precision and scale, which makes it the type for amounts and prices where rounding errors are not acceptable; in a URI it is written as digits with a decimal point followed by the suffix M or m, for example 2.345M. Edm.DateTime represents a date and time (from midnight, January 1, 1753 A.D. through December 9999 A.D.); in a URI it is written as datetime'yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm[:ss[.fffffff]]', for example datetime'2000-12-12T12:00'. No spaces are allowed between datetime and the quoted part, and the datetime prefix is case-insensitive. These literal forms apply in URIs (key predicates, $filter, service operation parameters) and HTTP headers; payload formats define their own representation, for example JSON writes Edm.DateTime as "/Date(<ticks>)/".
keyPoints: Edm.Decimal: fixed precision and scale; URI literal 2.345M (suffix M or m).
Edm.DateTime: date and time; URI literal datetime'2000-12-12T12:00' (no space after datetime).
URI literal forms differ from payload formats (JSON uses "/Date(<ticks>)/" for Edm.DateTime).

examples.title: Literal forms used in $filter
examples.code:
Edm.Boolean   true | false
              /Products?$filter=Discontinued eq false

Edm.Decimal   [0-9]+.[0-9]+M|m
              /Products?$filter=Price gt 2.345M

Edm.DateTime  datetime'yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm[:ss[.fffffff]]'
              /Products?$filter=ReleaseDate gt datetime'2000-12-12T12:00'

questions.title: Which integer and floating-point primitive types does OData V2 define, and how are their URI literals written?
questions.description: OData V2 defines four integer types and two binary floating-point types besides Edm.Decimal. Edm.Byte is an unsigned 8-bit integer and Edm.SByte a signed 8-bit integer; Edm.Int16, Edm.Int32 and Edm.Int64 are signed 16-, 32- and 64-bit integers. In URIs the integer types are plain digits with an optional minus sign, except Edm.Int64, which takes the suffix L (64L). Edm.Double is a floating-point number with 15 digits of precision (approximate range 2.23e-308 to 1.79e+308) and uses the suffix d, for example 2.029d or 1E+10d. Edm.Single is a floating-point number with 7 digits of precision and uses the suffix f, for example 2.0f. Use Double or Single for measured or scientific values where approximate precision is acceptable, and Decimal for exact values such as money. In the V2 JSON format, Edm.Int16 and Edm.Int32 are JSON numbers, while Edm.Int64, Edm.Byte, Edm.SByte, Edm.Double, Edm.Single and Edm.Decimal are written as JSON strings.
keyPoints: Int64 literal takes the suffix L: 64L.
Edm.Double (15 digits, suffix d: 2.029d) and Edm.Single (7 digits, suffix f: 2.0f).
Decimal for exact values (money), Double/Single for approximate values.
V2 JSON: Int16/Int32 are numbers; Int64, Byte, SByte, Double, Single and Decimal are strings.

examples.title: URI literal forms
examples.code:
Type          Literal form in a URI     Example
Edm.Byte      [0-9]+                    255
Edm.SByte     [-][0-9]+                 -8
Edm.Int16     [-][0-9]+                 -16
Edm.Int32     [-][0-9]+                 32
Edm.Int64     [-][0-9]+L                64L
Edm.Double    ...d                      1E+10d   2.029d
Edm.Single    [0-9]+.[0-9]+f            2.0f

questions.title: What are Edm.DateTimeOffset, Edm.Time, Edm.Guid, Edm.Binary and Null, and how are they written in a URI?
questions.description: Edm.DateTimeOffset represents a date and time together with its offset from GMT, so the time zone is part of the value; its literal is datetimeoffset'...' using the XML Schema datetime form with a time zone, for example 2002-10-10T17:00:00Z. Edm.Time represents a time of day (0:00:00 to 23:59:59), written as time'...' with an XML Schema dayTimeDuration such as PT13H20M. Edm.Guid is a 16-byte (128-bit) unique identifier, written as guid'dddddddd-dddd-dddd-dddd-dddddddddddd'. Edm.Binary is fixed- or variable-length binary data, written as X'23AB' or binary'23ABFF'; X and binary are case-sensitive, no space is allowed before the quote, and the hex digits must come in pairs. Null represents the absence of a value and is written null; OData has no ISNULL or COALESCE operators, so you compare with the null literal instead. In V2 JSON, Edm.Binary is a Base64 string, and DateTimeOffset, Time and Guid are their URI literal forms as JSON strings.
keyPoints: Edm.DateTimeOffset: date/time plus offset from GMT, e.g. 2002-10-10T17:00:00Z.
Edm.Time: time of day as a duration, time'PT13H20M'.
Edm.Binary: X'23AB' or binary'23ABFF' (case-sensitive prefix, hex pairs); Base64 string in JSON.
Null: literal null, used in comparisons such as eq null.

examples.title: URI literal forms
examples.code:
Edm.DateTimeOffset  datetimeoffset'2002-10-10T17:00:00Z'
Edm.Time            time'PT13H20M'
Edm.Guid            guid'12345678-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-ddddeeeeffff'
Edm.Binary          X'23AB'   or   binary'23ABFF'
Null                null      e.g. /Products?$filter=DiscontinuedDate eq null
